ch01.summary.domicia.0: Domícia was condemned by the College and walked ahead of the guards, as if she were leading them.
ch01.summary.domicia.1: Domícia remains Chief Vestal. Lívia knows what it cost.
ch01.summary.livia.0: Lívia stayed before the dogs, cup raised. The College took her.
ch01.summary.livia.1: Lívia went through the Gate, into a dark no fire of Vesta had ever reached.
ch01.summary.livia.2: Lívia carried temple fire to the port. She met a man no one remembers.
ch01.summary.livia.3: Lívia went down under the altar and saw three portals. One of them has nothing written on it.
ch01.summary.livia.4: Lívia stayed in the Temple, watching the flame until dawn.
ch01.summary.mirto.0: Mirto died on the stairs, the lamp in his hands.
ch01.summary.mirto.1: Mirto was taken alive by the College, to explain a closed eye scratched on a shard.
ch01.summary.mirto.2: Mirto followed Asterion into the deep. His father thinks he is dead.
ch01.summary.mirto.3: Mirto is locked in at home. His father was warned in time, by a stranger.
ch01.summary.mirto.4: Mirto went home, and he will go back to the galleries with bread.
ch01.summary.quinto.0: Quinto died in the galleries. No one found the monster's hair.
ch01.summary.quinto.1: Quinto lives, wounded. He will always remember the half of the blow that never came.
ch01.summary.quinto.2: Quinto lives. He came out of the galleries following knocks on the wall, and tells no one.
ch01.summary.quinto.3: Quinto lives, and tells everyone the monster is real.
ch01.summary.asterion.0: Asterion is not alone on the other side of the Gate.
ch01.summary.asterion.1: In Asterion, the beast now speaks louder than the man.
ch01.summary.asterion.2: Asterion is alone behind the Gate, his hand on the bronze.
ch01.summary.nerea.0: Nerea died at her mending stall. The net was left with a name sewn into the stitch.
ch01.summary.nerea.1: Nerea was taken alive by the College. She folded the net before she went, like someone who means to come back.
ch01.summary.nerea.2: Nerea left the city for a few days, because he asked. She still owes him a fish.
ch01.summary.nerea.3: Nerea still mends nets at the port, and still says his name.
ch01.summary.iante.0: Iante forgot she ever had a son.
ch01.summary.iante.1: Iante no longer expects anything from anyone.
ch01.summary.iante.2: Iante got her house key back, from the hand of the man who asked for it.
ch01.summary.iante.3: Iante still waits on the quay for the key she lent.
ch01.summary.theron.0: There are still people who say Théron's name out loud.
ch01.summary.theron.1: The world can barely hold Théron anymore.
ch01.summary.theron.2: Few remember Théron, and he counts every one.
ch01.summary.colegio.0: The College is on alert: it heard the knocking, the monster and the swindles, and has put the pieces together.
ch01.summary.colegio.1: The College has begun to put the pieces together.
ch01.summary.colegio.2: The College still doesn't know what it is looking for.
ch01.summary.dion.0: The Temple's ember reached the port, and Iante's son could go.
ch01.summary.dion.1: The promised ember never reached Iante's hands.
ch01.summary.varrao.0: Lívia told the College: "It was me." The augur wrote it down, and smiled.
ch01.summary.varrao.1: The augur was shamed by a Vestal in front of them all. He does not forget a face.
ch01.summary.varrao.2: Lívia pointed to the book, and the book pointed to Domícia.
ch01.summary.copos.0: The College scribe lost silver at the cups. He remembers the game, not the face.
ch01.summary.copos.1: The merchant's wife lost silver at the cups, and swears the man had no face.
ch01.summary.copos.2: Bíbulo lost his silver at the cups and drank the rest. He remembers nothing; nobody finds that strange.
ch01.summary.copos.3: On that fair day, Théron took nothing from anyone.
ch01.summary.nerea.4: Nerea still mends nets at the harbor. She paid a coin to hear a lie, and thinks it was worth it.
